finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: list_users_sorted() concatenates the raw $_GET['sort'] into the query with no allowlist or escaping. A prepared statement cannot parameterize ORDER BY, and none is used here. An attacker can inject SQLite expressions, e.g. sort=(CASE WHEN (SELECT substr(password,1,1) FROM users)='a' THEN id ELSE name END), to extract data from any table by boolean or ordering side-channel. Stacked queries are not possible via PDO::query on SQLite, so the impact is read-only data disclosure. The file defines functions only and nothing in the repo calls list_users_sorted(), so this is exploitable only if a caller invokes it. The sibling list_users_safe() at line 9 shows the intended allowlist fix.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at list.php:6

trace.note: $sort is concatenated into the SQL string and run via PDO::query

finding.guards_checked: No validation, allowlist, or cast on $sort. No auth check anywhere in the file. list_users_safe() (line 10-12) has an allowlist but is a separate function, and list_users_sorted() does not use it. find_user() (line 16-17) is SAFE because it uses a prepared statement with a bound parameter.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 takes $_GET['sort'] and concatenates it into an ORDER BY query with no allowlist, unlike list_users_safe() at list.php:10-11; the only caveat is that nothing in the repo calls list_users_sorted(), so it is reachable only if a caller exists.
